full_judgment:
9. Mr. Khandker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule has con- tended that the Election Tribunal has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in allowing the application for amendment of the election petition after the statutory period of limitation for the purpose of declaring the election of the petitioner void and the learned District Judge has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in declaring the opposite party No.4 as Chairman of the said UpazilaParishad in place of the petitioner inasmuch as by allowing the belated application for amendment of the election petition. The nature and character of the election petition has been materially changed. The learned Advocate secondly, contended that the Election Tribunal as well as the learned District Judge acted illegally and without jurisdiction in not dismissing the election petition for want of cause of action after the office of the Chairman of the said Upazila has been declared vacant by operation of law. 

 16. Thus although the Election Tribunal has the limited jurisdiction to allow amendment of the election petition, it has no power to allow any amendment, so as to relate hack to the date of filing of the election petition. It is so because sub-rule (1)of Rule 44 prescribed the limitation of 30 days next after the publication of the result in the official Gazette to file an election petition and sub-rule (5) specifically provides that an election petition shall set forth the ground on which the petition is fixed and the relief sought. In other words the ground for the election petition and the relief sought must be stated within the period of limitation. 

 17. In the instant case by the amendment petition opposite party No.4 introduced fresh facts and prayed for different relief long after 30 days of the publication of the result of the election in the official gazette. As such the Election Tribunal has no authority to allow such amendment to give retrospective effect to the election petition long after the period of limitation prescribed by rule 44 of the said rules. Both the decisions reported in 38 D.L.R. 435 and 1981 B.L.D. 298 supports this view of our". Hence ware of the view that the Election Tribunal has acted illegally and without jurisdiction in allowing the application for amendment of the election petition. As such the declaration by the Election Tribunal as well as by the learned District Judge that the election of the petitioner was void cannot be sustained in law. 

 19. The learned District Judge without any scrutiny of the evidence upheld the finding of the Election Tribunal that the election or the returned candidate was void. The learned District Judge on consideration of the evidence found that out of 45 polling centres polling was peaceful in 11 centres and the election was vitiated by corrupt practice in the remaining 34 polling centres. The learned District Judge took the view that the Election Tribunal was wrong in directing fresh election since there was peaceful election in 11 polling centres and should have directed re-election in the remaining 34 centres but since the petitioner has been elected a member of the Parliament he cannot contest the election for the post of Chairman of the Upazila Parishad in view of the amendment of section 6 of Ordinance Nq.LIX of 1982 by Ordinance No. XXXIV of 1986 which came into force on 31.5.86. The learned District Judge rejecting the contention of the petitioner that the office of the Chairman of the Nalchity Upazila Parishad has become vacant by operation of law held that the opposite party No.4 was entitled to be declared as Chairman of the said Upazila Parishad as the petitioner became disqualified to be a contesting candidate. Repelling the contention that the amendment of the election petition beyond the period of limitation was illegal and without jurisdiction the learned District Judge declared the opposite party No.4 as the Chairman of the said Upazila Parishad on the basis of the amended prayer made in the election petition. In view of our finding that the amendment being beyond the statutory period was illegal and without jurisdiction the declaration made by the learned District Judge cannot be sustained in law. In as much as the only declaration that could be made is that the election was void as a whole.
